name: Air Fryer Beef Empanadas with Black Bean and Corn Salad

components.name: Beef Empanadas

ingredients.name: Eight raw empanada dough discs, approximately 50 g each
Beaten egg for sealing and glaze

steps: Cook the measured beef in a skillet until browned, breaking it into small pieces. Add onion, pepper and garlic and cook until softened.
Stir in tomatoes, tomato paste, olives, cumin, paprika and salt. Simmer until the filling is reduced and no longer watery, then cool fully before filling dough.
Lay out eight empanada discs. Divide filling evenly among them, fold into half-moons and seal edges with a fork. Brush with measured beaten egg and a light spray of oil.
Preheat air fryer to 180 C. Air fry empanadas in spaced batches for approximately 9-13 minutes, turning if required, until pastry is golden and beef filling is steaming hot.

Pack two empanadas per serving plus one quarter of the bean-corn salad. The source calls for cooked picadillo; this adaptation includes the FULL raw filling recipe. For the best texture, freeze unbaked empanadas and cook directly from frozen with a longer time as needed. Keep salad refrigerated only.

components.name: Black Bean & Corn Salad

ingredients.name: Cooked, drained black beans, weighed ready to use
Drained canned sweetcorn, weighed ready to use

steps: Combine the ready-cooked, drained black beans with drained sweetcorn, diced tomato, onion, lime and coriander. Do not cook the salad.

notes: Draft — needs Mirna review: not kitchen-tested yet; macros and cooked yields are estimates.

Skinnytaste supplies air fryer directions using previously prepared picadillo. UNHANGRY gives a fully quantified from-raw beef filling and increases the serving unit to two empanadas with a measured bean salad per person.
Planning: Secondary stovetop for beef picadillo. Source originally serves 8 with one smaller empanada each; UNHANGRY complete meal base is 4, with two empanadas each.
Freezer: unbaked empanadas freeze especially well; salad is for fresh chilled use
Dietary: Wheat and egg in pastry; check dough ingredients. No pork.
Keeps 3–4 days in the fridge (≤4°C); refrigerate within 2 hours (1 hour above 32°C) in shallow containers, freeze portions for later in the week, and reheat to at least 74°C.
